source_audit.exact_english_statement: Suppose that O is a coherent sheaf of left Noetherian rings. Then, for every injective O-module B and every x in X, B(x) is an injective O(x)-module.

checks: The theorem explicitly permits associative noncommutative rings with identity, unital restriction maps, and unital left modules; it does not silently inherit the commutative convention.
The self-contained left Baer argument uses the left ideal L={r in R | rz in M'} and the well-defined left-linear extension on M'+Rz.
For left generators a_i, the germ-lifting map is (r_i) -> sum r_i a_i, with coefficients on the left; the opposite product order is neither used nor claimed.
The local left coherence condition makes the image sheaf finitely presented after shrinking, and exactness of stalks identifies its stalk with the chosen left ideal.
The stalk-Hom comparison is proved only as an isomorphism of abelian groups by comparing kernels from a finite presentation; no nonexistent natural left-R action on internal Hom is asserted.
Extension by zero and its adjunction use only the left action. Stalkwise monicity embeds j_!F into R, and injectivity of I extends the local germ map to R.
The preserved commutative lemma follows because coherence is local under restriction and every finite-type submodule of a coherent module is coherent and finitely presented.
The fixed-point/local-hypothesis form implies the global Tohoku statement at every point and is strictly stronger.
